text:
Alex: heads up — CUST-472 reported p95 API latency from APAC to our /v1/generate endpoint jumped from 180ms to ~1.2s around 08:03 UTC. customer started an escalation.
Maria: looking at metrics now — we have a correlated spike in egress TLS handshake time from apac-pop-3 to eu-west-edge between 07:58–08:10 UTC. p99 is ~2.4s.
Sam: any config changes around that time? I see a partial rollout of the new route-affinity change at 07:50 but it was supposed to be canaryed only to internal.
Ira: Deploy bot shows the canary toggle reverted at 07:55. But traceroutes from apac-pop-3 show a change in next-hop (ASNs differ) starting 07:59. Could be upstream provider.
Alex: customer logs show repeated TLS renegotiation and handshake retries. They posted a curl with --trace.
Support-Bot: forwarded customer curl output -> attached (redacted). Shows handshake timeout then successful connection after retry.
Maria: running probes now: `make egress-probe REGION=apac-pop-3 TARGET=eu-west`
Maria: probe results: 80% of flows take path A until 07:58, then 60% switch to path B with extra 90ms of RTT and additional TLS RTT due to cross-zone hairpin.
Sam: path B includes an extra hop via partner AS 64555 that had recent BGP flaps in their NOC. I see community tags not matching our prefer lists — maybe our route prepends got ignored.
Ira: I opened AS ticket with partner NOC (ticket 2026-PR-98). They acknowledged flaps and are investigating.
Alex: mitigation options: 1) force-route apac-pop-3 -> eu-west via alt-exit for ~30min 2) expand local caching/edge affinity for these customers 3) ask customer to pin region to apac (temporary). Thoughts?
Sam: do 1) as immediate mitigation. I can push a soft route preference change and watch for regressions.
Maria: make sure to enable extra TLS keepalive window so KV cache isn't invalidated by handshake flaps. I'll flip the keepalive TTL to 120s for edge workers in apac-pop-3.
Ira: I'll coordinate with partner NOC and post updates when they have root cause.
Alex: Sam — please apply the soft preference now and post the command you run. Also add a short rollback plan.
Sam: running command: `netops route-prefer --from apac-pop-3 --to eu-west --via alt-exit --weight 900 --expires 30m`
Sam: command succeeded, policy id `rp-3011-temp`; monitoring dashboards show dropback to baseline p95 after 45s. :thumbsup:
Maria: TLS handshake p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 210ms for affected flows. Traces show fewer cross-zone handoffs.
Support-Bot: notifying customer that we've applied a temporary routing preference and investigating upstream. Suggested message: "We've applied a temporary routing preference to reduce latency for your requests. This should restore most requests to normal p95; we will follow up when we have partner updates." Approve?
Alex: send that + offer a temporary region pin (apac) and a support call if they want deeper logs.
Ira: partner NOC just replied: BGP flap caused route withdrawal, then their internal dampening kicked longer than expected. They're rolling a fix and will confirm when stable.
Maria: postmortem items: - add probe for route affinity changes (alert when >10% shift) - ensure canary toggles are limited to internal prefixes only - add synthetic TLS handshake metric on apac pops - document rollback steps for netops route-prefer
Alex: assigning actions: Sam -> schedule permanant pref if partner doesn't stabilize in 4h; Maria -> PR for keepalive TTL change + add synthetic metric; Ira -> follow partner ticket and CC customer.
Sam: noted. I'll also add a short runbook snippet under eng-sre/networking: how to use `route-prefer` safely.
Support-Bot: customer informed and acknowledged, will keep case open.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-384 (edge-routing-p95-apac) assigned to eng-sre oncall.
Ira: thanks team. I'll update this thread when partner confirms fix.
Alex: thanks — great quick response.
Maria: one more note — observed a secondary ~5% error-rate bump for auth tokens during the spike (401s) likely due to handshake timeouts causing retries. We should correlate with auth service but looks transient.
Sam: watching auth logs, no persistent token invalidation — most are retries due to connection reset.
Alex: OK, we'll keep monitoring + follow up with postmortem tomorrow. :calendar:
